doc: Opposing (antagonist) functional groups for the name card's ADD menu. Group ids are the Q298 functional groups (data/derived/Q298_relations_<page>.json fgroups, identical on both Base pages) plus the groups defined here under added_groups (members are page-id bases; the sidecar adds _l / _r). Pairs are undirected (A opposes B and B opposes A). Every pair cites the book statement it rests on (printed page, paraphrase only). Built by scripts/anatomy/q368/build_antagonists_q368.py.

q368_toes_mtp_flex.name: Flexion of the lateral four toes at the metatarsophalangeal joints

refs.note: Metatarsophalangeal joints: flexion by flexor digitorum brevis, the lumbricals and the interossei (prime movers), with flexor digitorum longus and flexor accessorius (quadratus plantae) assisting.

q368_toes_mtp_flex.why: The Q298 set has extension at the 2nd-4th MTP joints but no flexion group for those toes.

q368_toes_ip_ext.name: Extension of the lateral four toes at the interphalangeal joints

refs.note: Interphalangeal joints of the foot: the digits are extended by extensor digitorum longus and brevis and extensor hallucis longus; the hallux muscle is split off into its own group here.

q368_toes_ip_ext.why: The Q298 set has flexion at the PIP / DIP joints of the 2nd-5th toes but no extension group.

q368_hallux_ip_ext.name: Extension of the great toe at the interphalangeal joint

refs.note: Interphalangeal joints of the foot: extensor hallucis longus is the long extensor named for the great toe in the extension list.

q368_hallux_ip_ext.why: The Q298 set has flexion at the great toe's IP joint but no extension group.

none.act_cervical_lat_p: Lateral flexion to one side is opposed by the same muscles of the other side, which are already in this group (it holds both sides); there is no separate opposing group.
none.act_cervical_rot_n: The two spinal rotation groups split rotation to the same side and to the opposite side, each holding both sides -- the right member of one and the left member of the other turn the same way, so they are not antagonists; the opposing rotation is produced by the same groups' members of the other side.

none.anterolateral_abdominal_wall: Grouped by region: rectus abdominis flexes the vertebral column (Mannan 2017 p. 311) while transversus abdominis only compresses the abdomen; the trunk-flexion action groups carry the pair with the erector spinae.
none.calcaneal_tendon_contributors: Defined by a shared tendon (calcaneal), not by an action; the plantarflexion groups carry the pair.
none.carpal_tunnel_contents: Defined by a shared tunnel (tendons and a nerve), not by an action.
none.gluteal: Mixed actions: gluteus maximus is the prime extensor of the hip, gluteus medius and minimus abduct and medially rotate it (Mannan 2017 pp. 296-297); the opposing groups are given per action instead.
none.hypothenar: Grouped by region (the short muscles of the little finger) with mixed actions; no opposing group.
none.itb_tensors: Defined by a shared insertion (the iliotibial tract), not by an action at one joint.
none.patellar_tendon_contributors: Defined by a shared tendon (quadriceps / patellar), not by an action; Quadriceps femoris carries the pair.
none.pes_anserinus: Defined by a shared insertion (the three medial knee tendons), not by an action.
none.rotator_cuff: Stabiliser group: it holds the humeral head in the glenoid, and its own members rotate in opposite directions (subscapularis medially; infraspinatus, teres minor laterally -- Mannan 2017 p. 196).
none.rotator_cuff_plus: Stabiliser group with the structures it runs under (see Rotator cuff); no opposing group.
none.scalenes: Grouped by region; their actions (flexing and side-bending the neck, raising the upper ribs) have no single opposing group.
none.suboccipital: Postural group that steadies and extends the head (Sontakke 2023 p. 225); no opposing group.
none.thenar: Grouped by region (the short muscles of the thumb) with mixed actions; the opposing movements are given per joint in the thumb action groups.
